content: Administer 5 mg orally once daily. Initiate treatment as early as possible after the onset of menses, but no later than 7 days after menses begins. The recommended total duration of treatment is 24 months. The safety and efficacy of this regimen have not been fully established. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Acitretin decreases the effects of norethindrone through an unknown mechanism. This combination is contraindicated, as it may result in contraceptive failure. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can reduce the exposure of drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as needed. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives coadministered with belzutifan may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Brigatinib induces CYP3A4 in vitro, and coadministration with hormonal contraceptives may result in decreased concentrations and loss of efficacy. Brigatinib may cause fetal harm. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not a reliable method of effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, and coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Hormonal contraceptives are not a reliable method of effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust the dose as necessary. Lesinurad decreases the effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Use additional methods of nonhormonal contraception, as hormonal contraception alone is not reliable when taking lesinurad. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor response to estrogens and progestins when a CYP3A4 inducer is added or discontinued, and adjust hormone dosage as necessary. Advise additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control during coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers and beyond discontinuation for approximately three plasma half-lives. Hormonal contraceptives are not a reliable method of effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mavacamten may decrease systemic exposures of ethinyl estradiol and progestin, potentially leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method not affected by CYP450 enzyme induction (e.g., intrauterine system) or add nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during coadministration and for 4 months after the last dose. Use of nonhormonal contraceptives is advised. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not a reliable method of effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Sugammadex sodium decreases the effects of norethindrone by receptor binding competition. A sugammadex bolus dose is considered equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives containing estrogen or progestogen. If an oral contraceptive is taken on the same day as sugammadex, or the patient has a transdermal or implant hormonal contraceptive, the patient must use an additional, nonhormonal contraceptive method (e.g., condoms and spermicides) for the next 7 days. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Topiramate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives are not a reliable method of effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects (e.g., amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, menorrhagia). Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates, where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Atazanavir may increase or decrease levels of norethindrone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer; effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be diminished when given concurrently. Additional nonhormonal forms of contraception are recommended. Colesevelam decreases levels of norethindrone by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer oral contraceptives containing norethindrone/ethinyl estradiol at least 4 hours before colesevelam to avoid decreased absorption. Crofelemer increases levels of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elagolix decreases levels of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered. Consider increasing CYP3A substrate dose if needed. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Fosamprenavir has an unspecified interaction mechanism with norethindrone. Use caution and monitor closely. Variable effects on norethindrone may occur. Use nonhormonal contraception. Iloperidone increases levels of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Norethindrone decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Norethindrone decreases the effects of insulin degludec/insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Norethindrone decreases the effects of inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of norethindrone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Norethindrone decreases the levels or effects of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. Combination oral contraceptives have been shown to significantly decrease plasma concentrations of lamotrigine.
